argv:
Workspace search shows things that were deleted and misses things that are back. Support collected these reports:

1. After an issue is archived, the issue itself no longer turns up in search, but its comments still do, and clicking one leads to an archived issue.
2. After an admin archives a whole project, the project disappears from search, but its issues and all of their comments are still found. This happens whether or not the admin chose to archive the project's issues as well. When the issues were kept, comments posted on them afterwards and edits made to them afterwards show up in search too.
3. When an archived project is restored, it never comes back in search, and neither do the issues and comments that had been kept.
4. Support ran the "rebuild search index" job for an affected workspace to clean this up. It made things worse: archived issues, deleted comments and the content of archived projects came back. In a large workspace, older issues and their comments were still missing after the rebuild. Entries that should not be there survived it.

The rule search must follow: a project can be found while it is live. An issue can be found while the issue and its project are both live. A comment can be found while the comment, its issue and that issue's project are all live. Search results and their reported total must follow this rule at all times: through archiving and restoring, and through comments and edits made at any time. Restoring a project does not restore issues that were archived, whether they were archived with the project or on their own before it, so those issues and their comments stay hidden. A rebuild of one workspace's index must leave exactly the entries the rule allows for all of that workspace's content, however large the workspace is, and it must not touch any other workspace's entries.
